action_history.rationale: Model: Sum of 13 Lorentzian-dominated pseudo-Voigt peaks (eta seeded ~0.8) on a constant+linear baseline, fit simultaneously over the full 109-1271 cm-1 range via TRF (Levenberg-Marquardt-style) least squares. Seed centers: ~120(shoulder), 130, 205, 262, 356, 402, 450(shoulder), 464, 505, 700, 810, 1085, 1160 cm-1. Dropped the spurious ~415 candidate; added a 120 cm-1 shoulder on the 130-band low flank and a 450 cm-1 shoulder on the 464-band rising flank to resolve the asymmetric composite line shapes. band_700 FWHM upper bound widened to 55 cm-1. No ALS subtraction (rolling-min baseline area fraction = 0.192, not fluorescence-dominated); background modeled as constant+linear parameters. Center windows +/-10 cm-1 (shoulders tighter: 116-124 and 445-455), FWHM 2-40 cm-1, amp>=0, eta in [0,1].

result.detailed_analysis: Band summary (center cm-1, relative intensity, strongest first): 464.0 (1.00, sharp, eta~0.89), 203.4 (0.32, broad FWHM ~27), 127.5 (0.24), 454-455 shoulder (0.15), 124 shoulder (0.09), 354.3 (0.08), 263.4 (0.07), 507.6 (0.03), 807.6 (0.03), 393.4 (0.02), 1081.1 (0.015), 1158.8 (0.012), 691.6 (0.007). The dominant sharp 464 cm-1 band (FWHM ~9.6 cm-1, center error 0.01 cm-1) is diagnostic of the alpha-quartz A1 symmetric Si-O-Si bending mode. The broad 205 cm-1 band and sharp 128, 356, 394, 507 cm-1 features complete the quartz lattice/framework mode pattern (positions match alpha-quartz within a few cm-1: 128, 206, 265, 355, 394, 464, 507). This is a multi-band, multi-intensity match (not just the strongest band), so the quartz assignment is well supported. The 262 cm-1 band is a known quartz weak mode. The residual bands are NOT explained by quartz: 1085 cm-1 with 155/282-region lattice modes would suggest a carbonate nu1 (calcite/aragonite ~1085-1086), but the required strong 712/282 or 705/206 companions are not clearly resolved above the quartz bands, so a carbonate accessory is only tentative; 807 cm-1 is near the olivine/silicate region but lacks its diagnostic pair; 700 and 1160 cm-1 are weak and broad. These minor bands most plausibly indicate a low-abundance secondary silicate/carbonate phase or amorphous/defect contributions, but none forms a complete secondary fingerprint on its own. Baseline is linear with small slope (0.0166) and rolling-min area fraction 0.192, confirming no fluorescence domination. Center parameters for strong bands are exceptionally well constrained; eta values pinned at 0 or 1 on shoulders/weak bands indicate those lineshapes are not independently determined.

scientific_claims.claim: The dominant Raman band at 464.0 +/- 0.01 cm-1 (FWHM 9.58 +/- 0.04 cm-1, eta 0.885) together with bands at 127.5, 203.4, 263.4, 354.3, 393.4, and 507.6 cm-1 identifies the sample as alpha-quartz (SiO2), with weak accessory bands at 700-1160 cm-1 indicating a minor secondary phase.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: A full multi-band match (positions and relative intensities) rather than a single-line match provides a robust mineralogical identification; the well-constrained 464 cm-1 position and width can serve as a crystallinity/strain indicator for quartz in the specimen.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone characterized quartz identification and crystallinity from the 464 cm-1 A1 mode position and width alongside a minor accessory phase in the 700-1160 cm-1 region?

verification_iterations.model: Sum of pseudo-Voigt profiles (Lorentzian-weighted, eta ~0.7-1.0) on a constant+linear baseline (no ALS; background is <40% of area). Start with 12 components: ~130, 205, 262, 356, 402, ~415 (weak broad feature seen in the 399-436 zoom), 464, 505, 700, 810, 1085, 1160 cm-1. Keep the ~415 component only if it survives fitting with amplitude above the noise floor; drop it if it parks on noise. I(x) = b0 + b1*x + Sum_i A_i*pseudoVoigt(x; x0_i, w_i, eta_i).

issues.location: ~450 cm-1 (rising edge of the 464 band, region 399.4–472.1)
issues.problem: The main 464 peak is under-resolved: the data shows a distinct shoulder/inflection on its low-frequency rising flank (~448–455) that the single Lorentzian at 463.4 does not cover.
Asymmetry of the 464 band is not captured; the fit overshoots the apex and falls too slowly on the descending flank.
The 130 band is under-resolved on its low-frequency side; the fit misses a shoulder near ~119–120 and mis-tracks the apex.

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Add a component seeded at ~450 cm-1 on the rising flank of the 464 band (and let band_130 relax/add a ~120 cm-1 shoulder) to resolve the systematic residual structure; drop or re-seed the noise-fitting band_415 candidate.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of pseudo-Voigt profiles (Lorentzian-weighted, eta ~0.7-1.0) on a constant+linear baseline (no ALS; background is <40% of area). I(x) = b0 + b1*x + Sum_i A_i*pseudoVoigt(x; x0_i, w_i, eta_i). Component set updated: retain the core bands at ~130, 205, 262, 356, 402, 464, 505, 700, 810, 1085, 1160 cm-1. DROP the spurious ~415 candidate (peak_6), which refined to noise-level amplitude (8.7 ± 9.8), center pinned at its 405 bound, and eta~0. ADD a shoulder component at ~450 cm-1 on the low-frequency rising flank of the 464 band to resolve its documented shoulder/inflection and reproduce the band's asymmetric line shape via the composite of the 450 + 464 pair. ADD (or re-seed) a shoulder component at ~120 cm-1 on the low-frequency flank of the 130 band to capture the under-resolved 119-120 shoulder. Net component count moves from 12 to ~13 (drop 415, add 450 and 120; band_130 either relaxes or gains a shoulder).
